title: HOTA: Hamiltonian framework for Optimal Transport Advection
claim: Our method transports source distributions to targets along optimal, feasible trajectories that bend around obstacles, on both smooth and non-smooth cost landscapes.
layout: 2x3 grid of scatter and trajectory plots; top row smooth costs, bottom row non-smooth; axes with tick labels; no arrows or captions inside panels
description: Six 2D scatter plots in a 2x3 grid on a pale background. Each panel has a blue potential field that marks high-cost regions. The top row shows smooth fields: two elongated Gaussian blobs, a narrow funnel (the Vneck), and a ring of small blobs. The bottom row shows non-smooth fields: slanted slit barriers, a vertical wall with a gap, and a solid dark square box. Red points are the source distribution. Black points are the target. Green points are the mapped samples, and they overlap the targets closely. Thin pastel dashed trajectories connect red to green and curve around the obstacles. In the 8-mode panel the paths fan out radially from a central red cluster to green clusters. The eye goes first to the dark blue obstacles and the colorful path bundles. A section heading, '5.2 Comparative Evaluation on Two-Dimensional Data', is cropped in above the plots.
caption: Evaluation of HOTA method on smooth (top) and non-smooth datasets (bottom): Stunnel, Vneck, GMM, BabyMaze, Slit, Box. Blue regions indicate high values of potential $U(x)$. Distributions $\alpha$ (red), $\beta$ (black) and the mapped $T_\#\alpha$ (green).
abstract: Optimal transport (OT) has become a natural framework for guiding the probability flows. Yet, the majority of recent generative models assume trivial geometry (e.g., Euclidean) and rely on strong density-estimation assumptions, yielding trajectories that do not respect the true principles of optimality in the underlying manifold. We present Hamiltonian Optimal Transport Advection (HOTA), a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman based method that tackles the dual dynamical OT problem explicitly through Kantorovich potentials, enabling efficient and scalable trajectory optimization. Our approach effectively evades the need for explicit density modeling, performing even when the cost functionals are non-smooth. Empirically, HOTA outperforms all baselines in standard benchmarks, as well as in custom datasets with non-differentiable costs, both in terms of feasibility and optimality.
